sources.excerpt: Fictional patient DEMO-58 is a 58-year-old woman weighing 68 kg.
On 5 October 2026 she developed bilateral thigh muscle pain and weakness while taking atorvastatin.
I suspect atorvastatin; causality is not established.
She was hospitalized from 5 to 6 October 2026.
No death, life-threatening event, disability, congenital anomaly, intervention to prevent permanent impairment or other serious outcome applied.

Atorvastatin was prescribed for hyperlipidemia, started on 20 September 2026, generic 20 mg tablets, administered as 20 mg by mouth once daily, fictional manufacturer Example Pharma, lot DEMO-AT20-01.
Creatine kinase was 1450 U/L on 5 October 2026 and 320 U/L on 8 October 2026, each with reference range 30 to 200 U/L.
Relevant history is hypertension and hyperlipidemia, with no known drug allergies.
Lisinopril 10 mg by mouth once daily for hypertension started on 1 June 2026; it is concomitant, not suspect.
Adverse event
Atorvastatin was stopped on 5 October 2026.
Its dose was not reduced.
The muscle pain and weakness improved after stopping it.
Atorvastatin was never restarted.
The patient received intravenous fluids and was discharged on 6 October 2026.
By 10 October 2026 the symptoms had resolved.
Outcome: recovered.
Lisinopril was continued unchanged.
The clinician declined to provide reporter details.
Date of this report: 2026-10-17.
